evidence_note: Adhyaya 1, Pada 1 of the Jaimini Upadesa Sutra, encoded from two independent witnesses read in the original: K. V. Abhyankar's 1951 critical edition (15 manuscripts, with his English translation) and the Jaiminiyasutram with the Sutrarthaprakasika Sanskrit commentary (DLI 2015.242319). The two agree on the substance of every rule encoded here and disagree on sutra NUMBERING by exactly one from 1.1.15 onward, because Abhyankar's text carries a Pitrkaraka sutra the Sutrarthaprakasika's does not. Both numberings are recorded on every affected rule. Sanskrit was read directly; no modern copyrighted translation was relied on. Grade for the engine's own renderings is engine_translation_unreviewed. Nothing here is customer-eligible: there is no Jaimini engine, no independent Sanskrit review, and no reproduced worked example yet.

conditions.candidate_set: the seven grahas Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn (Rahu optionally, see the scheme rules)
conditions.measure: longitude within the occupied sign, i.e. sidereal longitude modulo 30 degrees

conclusion.atmakaraka: the graha with the greatest degrees-within-sign
conclusion.arithmetic: rank descending on (degree, minute, second) of longitude mod 30
conclusion.tie_break_primary: kaladibhih - if degrees are equal, compare minutes, then finer units
conclusion.note: This is pure arithmetic and is directly implementable and testable. It is the single most implementable rule in the text.
conclusion.divergence_from_parasari: Parasari karakas are FIXED by nature (Sun = father, Moon = mother, ...). Jaimini's chara karakas are assigned per chart by degree, so the same graha signifies different topics in different nativities.
